fact: Algeria launched its first national AI and cybersecurity start-up cluster on 18 April 2026 at the Sidi Abdellah science and technology hub in Algiers, backed by the Higher Education, Knowledge Economy and Telecommunications ministries; no cohort is named.
El Watan says the network of Maisons de l'IA serves as hubs for awareness and socio-economic partnership, with no incubation programme stated.

The minister inaugurated a drone design and piloting platform meant to take in 20 new drone start-ups by the end of 2025 and reach 100 start-ups a year from 2027, with technical and financial support.
The Algerian Space Agency (ASAL) inaugurated its incubator, with ENSIA and ENSM, at the Sidi Abdellah science and technology hub on 17 October 2025; no cohort or programme is described.
Finance Law 2025 extends incubators' IRG/IBS exemptions two years subject to label renewal, per Deloitte Société d'Avocats; no programme or cohort stated.
The incubator Advalians, with Algeria Venture and the startups ministry, runs a 12-month Kick Start 2025 incubation programme for 8 selected project holders.
Ooredoo Algerie says its T-Start incubation programme, running since 2013, has incubated 72 startups, has 21 incubated now, and took four more on 23 December 2025.
The Ministry of Post and Telecommunications page says the Sidi-Abdellah cyberpark incubator supports young entrepreneurs and startups with training, workshops, workspace and coaching.
The ministry page says incubators operate at Sidi-Abdellah, Bordj Bou Arréridj and Oran.
The ministry page says the Sidi-Abdellah cyberpark is in operation and currently hosts over thirty companies.
